Cc: AlphaHealth Procurement <procurement@alphahealth.com>

Subject: Clarify Dedicated pricing structure and remedy triggers

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement has a few follow-ups on the Dedicated pricing proposal you sent over. Specifically:

- We need a clearer definition of what constitutes a 'Capacity Unit' in the proposal (is it GPU-hours, reserved vGPUs, or concurrent inference slots?).
- How are throughput guarantees measured? Are they per-pool or per-model? What happens if our workload patterns (spiky daytime traffic) cause short-term throttles?
- The SLA remedy matrix references 'service credits' but doesn't show the trigger windows (monthly availability vs 5-min P95 events). Can you provide exact trigger conditions and examples?

We want to avoid ambiguity before legal reviews the MSA. If you can send a short redline of the remedy language and the pricing matrix with definitions, that would be ideal.

Best,
Jen
Procurement Lead, AlphaHealth

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jen Park <jen.park@alphahealth.com>
Cc: AlphaHealth Procurement <procurement@alphahealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-28T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify Dedicated pricing structure and remedy triggers

Hi Jen —

Thanks for the clear list. I'm attaching an updated pricing matrix (v2) and a suggested redline for the SLA remedies. Quick summary up front so your legal/procurement team can scan:

- "Capacity Unit": defined in the spreadsheet as a "Reserved GPU Unit (RGU)" which maps to a normalized GPU-hour equivalent based on model family and quantization profile. We include a conversion table so you can see how many RGUs typical LLMs consume for your expected throughput.
- "Throughput Guarantees": expressed as both a per-pool steady-state throughput (requests/sec at 95th percentile under steady traffic) and a burst allowance (short windows where autoscaling/burst capacity applies). We propose measuring throughput at the pool ingress (per-customer pool) using 1-minute aggregation windows and P95 over the billing month for SLA evaluation.
- "SLA Remedies": service credits triggered by monthly pool availability and by sustained P95 latency breaches. The draft shows a three-tier ladder (<=99.5%, 99.0-99.5%, <99.0%) with percentage credits of monthly committed fees. For very short spikes we propose a threshold (latency breach must persist for >= 10 consecutive 1-minute windows to qualify).

I'll loop in Karthik on the definitions and Ben on discount cadence so we can propose concrete redline wording your counsel can review.

Next steps: I'll circulate an internal ask for legal wording and send you a DocuSign link once we have agreement on the numeric values.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_Pricing_Matrix_v2.xlsx, Suggested_SLA_Remedies_Redline.docx

Team — forwarding AlphaHealth's procurement note plus the matrix I attached. Key asks we need to resolve before sending final redline:

1) Capacity Unit naming and conversion: our spreadsheet uses "RGU (Reserved GPU Unit)" and a conversion to GPU-hour equivalent. Legal often pushes back on metric ambiguity; can we tighten the language to explicitly reference the conversion table and say the conversion is used "solely for billing and capacity planning"?

2) Throughput measurement window: I suggested 1-minute aggregation with monthly P95 evaluation. Karthik — is that robust for their spiky traffic? Can we propose an autoscale-burst carve-out (e.g., first 5 minutes of a daily spike are not penalized)?

3) Remedy ladder: They want examples. Ben — can you propose discount tiers and whether we can offer an initial 10% implementation credit if they accept a 12-month reserved commit? That might help move legal faster.

Please reply with exact language we can drop into the SLA redline docx. AlphaHealth is hoping to get legal review started by Friday.

Thanks —
Marissa

Marissa / Ben —

Thanks for the context. A few concrete suggestions to reduce ambiguity and protect both sides:

- Capacity Unit: change the definition to: "Reserved GPU Unit (RGU): a billing unit equal to one GPU-hour normalized to a baseline model family (Baseline = 16GB FP16 A100-equivalent). The RGU conversion table in Appendix A shall govern conversions for other model families/quantization profiles. Conversion factors are applied only for billing and capacity planning and do not alter functional behavior of the service."

- "Throughput Guarantees": measure at the pool-level ingress as Marissa suggested. Use 1-minute aggregation windows and compute P95 over the billing month. Add an explicit "Burst Allowance" clause: "Each pool is entitled to up to 300% of steady-state throughput for aggregate burst durations not exceeding 120 minutes per billing month; bursts beyond this will be measured against committed capacity and may incur overage charges."

- SLA Remedy Triggers: propose that only month-level availability (calendar-month) and sustained latency breaches (>= 10 consecutive 1-minute windows) trigger credits. Keep short one-off spikes (sub-10 windows) out unless they accompany an availability incident. List example calculations in Appendix B.

I'll add this wording to the draft docx and attach. If Ben can confirm the discount cadence (12-month commit with staggered ramp) I'll add the implementation credit language.

Karthik
Product, Redwood Inference
